quizzes.title: Key terms and ideas
quizzes.intro: Ten quick checks on reed numbering, denting and preparatory limits.

questions.q: The Stockport sett of a reed is the number of
options: ends per inch in the fabric
questions.explain: Stockport reeds are numbered by dents in two inches; dents per inch is half of it and dents per metre is the modern system.

questions.q: Why does the Stockport number equal the ends per inch in the reed for so many fabrics?
options: Because most reeds have one end per dent
Because with two ends per dent, dents per 2 in × 2 ends = ends per inch
Because the reed is two inches deep
questions.explain: Two ends in each dent over two inches of reed is the same count as ends in one inch, which made the number convenient for plain-weave mills.

questions.q: A reed marked 1230 in the metric system has
questions.explain: Metric reeds are numbered by dents per metre; 1,230 ÷ 39.37 = 31.24 dents per inch.

questions.q: Fewer ends per dent generally give a cleaner fabric with fewer reed marks.
questions.explain: Crowding many ends in a dent leaves gaps between dents (reediness); spreading the ends over more dents hides the reed.

questions.q: The denting rule recommends putting in each dent
options: one repeat of the weave, or a simple fraction of it
exactly two ends whatever the weave
questions.explain: Plain weave takes its 2-end repeat, 2/1 twill its 3, 3/1 twill its 4; this keeps the interlacing pattern aligned with the dents.

questions.q: A five-end satin is dented 2, 3, 2, 3 … ends per dent, so on average it has
questions.explain: Alternating 2 and 3 gives 5 ends in two dents, that is 2.5 per dent — the value used in the worksheet (80.4 EPI).

questions.q: 'Weft contraction' in the reed worksheet refers to
options: the shortening of weft yarn in the size box
the fabric being narrower than the reed width after weaving
the loss of weft in wastage
the fabric shrinking in the wash
questions.explain: Weft crimp pulls the cloth in from the reed width, so the fabric is narrower and the ends are closer than in the reed.

questions.q: The maximum number of ends a plant can warp is warper creel cones × sizing creel beams.
questions.explain: Each warper's beam carries at most one end per cone and the sizing creel takes a limited number of beams: 1,024 × 28 = 28,672 ends.

questions.q: The 28,672-end limit constrains
options: either the width or the density — their product cannot exceed it
questions.explain: Ends = EPI × width, so a dense fabric must be narrower and a wide fabric must be sparser.

questions.q: Following the denting rule, a 3/1 twill is dented with
questions.explain: The 3/1 twill repeats on four ends, so four ends go in each dent; three per dent is the 2/1 twill rule.

quizzes.title: Formulas and relationships
quizzes.intro: The conversions between reed systems and the formulas that link reed, denting and fabric EPI.

questions.q: Dents per inch from a metric reed number are
questions.explain: There are 39.37 inches in a metre, so dividing dents per metre by 39.37 gives dents per inch.

questions.q: The Stockport sett is
questions.explain: Stockport counts dents in two inches, so it is twice the dents per inch: 31.24 × 2 = 62.5.

questions.q: Ends per inch in the finished fabric equal
options: dents/in × ends per dent ÷ (1 + weft contraction)
dents/in × ends per dent × (1 + weft contraction)
questions.explain: The reed sets the ends per inch at the reed; contraction squeezes the same ends into a narrower cloth, so EPI rises by (1 + contraction).

questions.q: The reed width that must be filled for a fabric of width W with weft contraction c is
questions.explain: The cloth comes off narrower than the reed, so the reed must be wider: 63 × 1.03 = 64.89 in.

questions.q: If the weft contraction turns out higher than assumed, the fabric EPI will be higher than planned for the same reed.
questions.explain: The same number of ends end up in a narrower cloth, so ends per inch increase.

questions.q: Maximum fabric width at a given EPI is
questions.explain: Width × EPI = ends, so width = 28,672 ÷ 200 = 143.4 in at 200 EPI.

questions.q: Maximum EPI at a given fabric width is
questions.explain: 28,672 ÷ 110 = 260.7 ends per inch at 110 in width.

questions.q: What is the Stockport sett of a 1230 dents-per-metre reed? Give one decimal.
questions.explain: 1230 ÷ 39.37 = 31.24 dents per inch; × 2 = 62.5 dents per two inches.

questions.q: Keeping the same reed and contraction but changing from 2 to 4 ends per dent
questions.explain: EPI is proportional to ends per dent: 64.4 becomes 128.7 in the worksheet.

questions.q: A coarse reed with few dents per inch can never produce a dense fabric.
questions.explain: More ends per dent let a coarse reed weave a dense fabric; the trade-off is a more visible reed mark.

quizzes.title: Worked calculations
quizzes.intro: Recreate the lecture's reed worksheet and the preparatory capacity figures.

questions.q: Convert a 1230 dents/m reed to dents per inch (1 m = 39.37 in). Give two decimals.
questions.explain: 1230 ÷ 39.37 = 31.24 dents per inch.

questions.q: A fabric is to be 63 in wide with 3 % weft contraction. What reed width must be filled, to two decimals?
Plain weave, 2 ends per dent, in a 31.24 dents/in reed with 3 % weft contraction. Ends per inch in the fabric, to one decimal?
questions.explain: 31.24 × 2 = 62.5 ends per inch in the reed; × 1.03 = 64.4 in the fabric.

questions.q: Same reed (31.24 dents/in) and 3 % contraction, but a 2/1 twill dented 3 ends per dent. Fabric EPI to one decimal?
Same reed and contraction, 4/1 satin dented 2, 3, 2, 3 (2.5 ends per dent average). Fabric EPI to one decimal?
A warper creel holds 1,024 cones and the sizing creel takes 28 beams. What is the maximum number of ends?
questions.explain: 1,024 ends per beam × 28 beams = 28,672 ends.

questions.q: With a maximum of 28,672 ends, what is the widest fabric possible at 200 ends per inch? Give one decimal.
With 28,672 ends, what is the maximum EPI for a 110 in wide fabric? Give one decimal.
A reed numbered 1600 dents/m has about how many dents per inch?
questions.explain: 1600 ÷ 39.37 = 40.6. 81.3 is the Stockport sett (× 2), and 63 comes from dividing by 25.4 as if converting mm.

questions.q: Which denting in the 1230 reed with 3 % contraction gives about 128.7 ends per inch?
questions.explain: 31.24 × 4 × 1.03 = 128.7. Three per dent gives 96.5 and two gives 64.4.

quizzes.title: Applied in practice
quizzes.intro: Reed-room and planning decisions: which reed, which denting, and whether the plant can make the warp at all.

questions.q: An order needs about 80 EPI in a plain-weave-like satin and the only reed in stock is 1230 dents/m (31.24 dents/in, 3 % contraction). You should
options: order a new reed — nothing else works
questions.explain: 2.5 ends per dent average gives 31.24 × 2.5 × 1.03 = 80.4 EPI. Three per dent gives 96.5 and two gives 64.4, both far off.

questions.q: A customer asks for a 150 in wide fabric at 200 EPI (30,000 ends) from a plant whose limit is 28,672 ends. The practical answer is
options: accept it — the sizing machine will manage
offer at most 143 in at 200 EPI, or 150 in at a lower EPI
run the warper at higher speed
questions.explain: Width × EPI must stay under 28,672: 28,672 ÷ 200 = 143.4 in, or 28,672 ÷ 150 = 191 EPI. Denting or speed do not change the end count.

questions.q: An order is 72 in wide at 220 ends per inch. How many ends does the warp need?
questions.explain: 72 × 220 = 15,840 ends — comfortably inside the 28,672 limit.

questions.q: With 1,024-cone creels, a 63 in fabric at 128 EPI (8,064 ends) can be made from 8 warper's beams.
questions.explain: 8 × 1,024 = 8,192 ends, which covers 8,064; 7 beams would give only 7,168.

questions.q: A plain fabric shows faint lengthwise lines matching the reed dents. The usual cause and fix is
options: too many ends per dent — use a finer reed with fewer ends per dent
too few ends per dent — crowd more ends per dent
weft contraction too low — loosen the weft
the reed is too wide — trim it
questions.explain: Reed marks come from gaps between dent groups; spreading the ends over more dents (fewer per dent) makes a cleaner cloth.

questions.q: A mill buys reeds marked Stockport 70. In dents per inch that is
questions.explain: Stockport counts two inches, so 70 ÷ 2 = 35 dents per inch.

questions.q: A fabric planned at 63 in comes off the loom at 61 in. The likely cause and remedy is
options: weft contraction higher than the 3 % assumed — use a wider reed space
too few ends per dent — add ends
the reed number is wrong — switch to Stockport
questions.explain: Width loss is weft contraction; if it is 6 % rather than 3 %, the reed must be filled wider (63 × 1.06 = 66.8 in) to land on 63 in.

questions.q: What reed width must be filled for a 60 in fabric if the weft contraction is 5 %?
questions.explain: 60 × 1.05 = 63 in of reed.

questions.q: A trainee counts four ends in each dent of a 31.24 dents/in reed and records the fabric EPI as 31.24 × 4 = 125. The missing step is
options: dividing by 2 for the Stockport system
questions.explain: 125 is the EPI in the reed; the cloth contracts 3 % in width, so the fabric EPI is 125 × 1.03 = 128.7.

questions.q: The Stockport sett equals the ends per inch in the reed only when the reed is dented with two ends per dent.
questions.explain: With three or four ends per dent the ends per inch in the reed are 1.5 or 2 times the Stockport number.

quizzes.title: Challenge review
quizzes.intro: Two-step reed problems and the comparisons that catch students out.

questions.q: A 1400 dents/m reed is dented 3 ends per dent and the weft contraction is 4 %. Fabric EPI to one decimal?
A plain fabric needs 100 EPI with 2 ends per dent and 3 % weft contraction. What reed number (dents per metre) is required, to the nearest whole dent?
A student reports 62.5 EPI for plain weave in the 1230 reed. This figure is
options: the ends per inch in the reed, before weft contraction
the Stockport sett for a 3-per-dent reed
questions.explain: 31.24 × 2 = 62.5 is the reed EPI (and happens to equal the Stockport sett); the fabric EPI is 62.5 × 1.03 = 64.4.

questions.q: A Stockport 64 reed is dented 2 ends per dent and the weft contraction is 3 %. Fabric EPI to one decimal?
questions.explain: Stockport 64 with 2 per dent = 64 ends per inch in the reed; × 1.03 = 65.9 in the fabric.

questions.q: A 63 in fabric at 128 EPI uses what fraction of a 28,672-end capacity?
questions.explain: 8,064 ÷ 28,672 = 0.281, so about 28 % of the maximum warp.

questions.q: With 28,672 ends available, what is the maximum EPI for a 90 in fabric? Give one decimal.
questions.explain: 28,672 ÷ 90 = 318.6 ends per inch.

questions.q: Reed A is 1230 dents/m with 3 ends per dent; reed B is 1845 dents/m with 2 ends per dent. For the same contraction, the fabric EPI is
questions.explain: Ends per metre in the reed: 1230 × 3 = 3,690 and 1845 × 2 = 3,690 — identical. Reed B will show less reediness, though.

questions.q: Denting a five-end satin with 5 ends in every dent follows the 'one repeat per dent' rule.
questions.explain: Five ends is exactly one repeat; the lecture's 2-3-2-3 alternative splits the repeat into simple fractions to reduce reed marks.

questions.q: Which change raises the maximum fabric width a plant can make at a given EPI?
options: A larger warper creel or more beams on the sizing creel
questions.explain: Maximum ends = cones × beams; only those two numbers raise the cap. Reed and denting change how the ends are spaced, not how many there are.

questions.q: A plant has 1,200-cone creels and a 30-beam sizing creel. What is its maximum fabric width at 250 EPI?
